newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up 2.25 pct on support hope.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up 2.25 pct on support hope.

text.p: Thai stocks closed sharply higher on Tuesday on expectations of possible support to Thailand from the International Monetary Fund and Japan and on bargain hunting in some discounted shares, brokers said.
The composite SET index finished 13.75 points or 2.25 percent up at 625.66. The SET-50 rose 1.29 points to 46.81.
"The market had a positive reaction to the IMF's possible help. Any help from foreign countries will be good for Thailand," said one broker at Nava Finance and Securities.
So far Thailand has only received technical aid from the IMF and has yet to ask the fund for other assistance.
Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Tuesday said he was committed to helping Thailand in conjuction with the IMF if necessary.
Trade remained thin on the exchange, with 195 million shares worth 4.2 billion baht changing hands.
Brokers said the fragile baht made foreign investors put their additional investments into the stock market.
Thai Farmers Bank gained two baht to 106 on the most active trade of 208 million baht.
